title: Optimize Automation API: idempotent apply / safe rollback for batching & KV-cache recommendations
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Goal: Add first-class API and SDK primitives for Redwood Optimize automation so platform recommendations for batching and KV/prefix caching can be safely applied, rolled back, and audited programmatically. This ticket covers an API surface, webhook model for events and long-running apply operations, idempotent apply semantics, optimistic locking/versioning, dry-run validation, and an SDK convenience layer.

Motivation and constraints:
- Customers will want programmatic automation to reduce unit cost: autobatching and cache policies may be applied to high-volume routes. These changes must never cause regressions in latency or QoE.
- Operations must be reversible and observable: we need strong audit trails, versioned policy objects, and safe rollback triggers (manual or automated on regressions).
- API calls must be idempotent to support retries from orchestrators (Airflow, Step Functions) and webhook event replays.
- Minimize blast radius: we should support staged rollout (canary route subset or percentage of traffic) and dry-run mode that simulates cost/latency impact.

Proposal (high level):
1) New resources and types:
   - /optimize/policies: CRUD for recommendation policies (JSON blobs with batching, cache, quantization hints, thresholds, eligibility selectors). Policies are versioned.
   - /optimize/operations: long-running apply/rollback operations. POST returns operation id; operations are idempotent keyed by client-provided idempotency_key.
   - /optimize/events (webhook subscription): subscribe to operation lifecycle events (created, started, progress, applied, rolled_back, failed), and evaluation alerts (regression_detected).

2) Idempotency & concurrency model:
   - Clients may provide idempotency_key on POST /optimize/operations. If the same client_id + idempotency_key pair is seen, the server returns the original operation resource rather than creating a duplicate.
   - Policy resources are immutable once applied: creating a new version creates {policy_id, version}. Apply operations reference a specific policy version.
   - Apply operations use optimistic concurrency via operation preconditions: if the live model/route config changed since plan generation, the operation fails with 409 and a diff payload.

3) Safe apply & rollback semantics:
   - Two-phase apply: plan -> dry-run -> apply. POST /operations?mode=plan returns a simulated plan with estimated token savings and latency delta.
   - Dry-run mode executes internal dry path (no route rewrites) and runs synthetic traffic/benchmarks against a copy of the policy to produce metrics.
   - Apply can be staged (percentage rollout or route selector). The operation updates status.progress and emits webhook events.
   - Automatic safeguard: if configured evaluation metrics (p99 latency, error rate, quality score on prompt-set) regress beyond thresholds during rollout, operation auto-pauses and triggers rollback.
   - Rollback is a first-class operation (POST /operations?action=rollback referencing operation_id). Rollbacks are idempotent and create a new operation resource for tracking.

4) Webhooks & notifications:
   - Webhook events include operation metadata, policy version, diffs, current rollout percentage, and metric snapshots. Payloads include an event_id to ensure at-least-once delivery handling by clients.
   - Retries: Redwood will retry webhooks with exponential backoff; clients should dedupe via event_id and idempotency keys.

5) SDK ergonomics (JS + Python):
   - optimize.create_policy(policy_json) -> returns policy_id, version
   - optimize.plan_apply(policy_id, options={dry_run:true}) -> plan summary
   - optimize.apply(policy_id, {idempotency_key, rollout:{percent:10}, eval_hooks:[...]} ) -> Operation object (pollable)
   - Operation.wait(timeout) auto-polls and surfaces errors; Operation.rollback() convenience method.
   - SDK handles idempotency header injection and exponential retry for transient 500/502 with jitter.

6) Auditability & tracing:
   - All apply/rollback operations write to an immutable operation log with actor (API key / user), timestamp, and policy diffs.
   - Integrate with Console -> per-route timeline view and operation playback.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- Synchronous vs async: applies are async to prevent timeouts on large fleets — users need a pollable operation resource.
- Dry-run fidelity: dry-run runs synthetic checks and model-latency estimates but can't guarantee 100% reproduction of production traffic; therefore default rollout uses a small canary.
- Strong consistency vs availability: optimistic checks may fail under rapid concurrent operations; we accept occasional 409 requiring client retry.

API spec snippets (draft):
POST /v1/optimize/policies
  Body: {"name":"aggressive-batching-routeX","selectors":{...},"settings":{"batching":{...},"kv_cache":{"enabled":true}}}
  Response: {"policy_id":"pol_...","version":"v1"}

POST /v1/optimize/operations
  Headers: Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
  Body: {"policy_id":"pol_...","policy_version":"v1","action":"apply","mode":"staged","rollout":{"percent":10},"dry_run":false}
  Response: {"operation_id":"op_...","status":"queued","idempotency_key":"..."}

GET /v1/optimize/operations/op_... -> operation resource with status, progress, events[]

Webhook event example (application/json):
{
  "event_id":"evt_...",
  "type":"operation.progress",
  "operation_id":"op_...",
  "policy_id":"pol_...",
  "meta":"{...}",
  "metrics":{"p99_latency_ms":420,"cost_delta":-0.12}
}

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency store, optimistic-lock checks, operation state machine.
- Integration tests: fake-route harness that validates dry-run vs canary vs full rollout; simulated regression triggers to validate auto-rollback.
- End-to-end QA: internal staging tenant with production-like traffic to validate metrics and webhook flows.
- Canary rollout: enable API in staging-> internal canary customers -> opt-in beta customers -> GA.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- Metric: time-to-complete apply ops (p50/p95), webhook delivery success rate, auto-rollback rate, number of 409 concurrency failures.
- Alerts: auto-rollback > 0.5% per day triggers ops review; webhook failure > 5% in 1h triggers incident.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default idempotency key timeframe: how long do we retain idempotency for (24h vs 7d)?
- Schema for policy selectors: need stable, expressive DSL for route matching (headers, path regex, customer tags).
- Rollout stop conditions: allow custom evaluation functions (server-side JS?) or restrict to metric thresholds.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Optimize+Automation+API+Spec
- Mock API contract (OpenAPI draft): https://drive.redwood.ai/optimize/openapi-draft.yaml
- GH PR (proto): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234
- Dry-run harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-dryrun

Acceptance criteria (must be met for Done):
- Endpoints implemented and covered by unit + integration tests.
- SDK methods implemented for JS + Python with idempotency handling.
- Webhook subscription and retry mechanism implemented; console shows operation timeline.
- Dry-run produces repeatable plans and canary rollout works with auto-rollback on regression.
- Security review completed and KMS/audit log integration verified.
